report:
### Conclusion
The health claim is **true**. High-quality evidence demonstrates that preoperative skin preparation with chlorhexidine–alcohol reduces the risk of surgical-site infections (SSIs) after cesarean delivery compared with iodine–alcohol or povidone–iodine preparations.

### Key Evidence
* **Randomized Controlled Trials:** A landmark randomized clinical trial published in the *New England Journal of Medicine* showed that preoperative skin antisepsis with chlorhexidine–alcohol significantly reduced the rate of SSIs following cesarean delivery compared to iodine–alcohol (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1511048). Another randomized trial comparing chlorhexidine–alcohol directly with povidone–iodine–alcohol observed a significantly lower SSI rate in the chlorhexidine group (6.95% vs. 14.28%) (https://www.ijrcog.org/index.php/ijrcog/article/view/6461).
* **Systematic Reviews & Meta-Analyses:** A systematic review and meta-analysis confirmed that preoperative skin cleansing with chlorhexidine–alcohol reduces SSIs in women undergoing cesarean section compared to povidone–iodine formulations (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30184558/). Additionally, a network meta-analysis evaluating antiseptics specifically for cesarean sections found that alcohol-based 2% chlorhexidine had the highest probability of being the most effective agent for preventing SSIs (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0195670124001282).

Overall, clinical evidence supports prioritizing chlorhexidine–alcohol over iodine-based skin antiseptics to prevent post-cesarean surgical-site infections.

### Sources
1. *New England Journal of Medicine* - Trial on skin antiseptic agents at cesarean delivery: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1511048
2. *International Journal of Reproduction, Contraception, Obstetrics and Gynecology* - Trial on chlorhexidine-alcohol vs povidone-iodine-alcohol: https://www.ijrcog.org/index.php/ijrcog/article/view/6461
3. *PubMed* - Systematic review and meta-analysis on preoperative skin antisepsis for cesarean delivery: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30184558/
4. *ScienceDirect* - Network meta-analysis on antiseptics for caesarean section: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0195670124001282
